_comment: Which parent zones to scrape subzone lore for, keyed by uiMapID.
Subzones are enumerated from 'Category:<name> subzones' on warcraft.wiki.gg;
set `category` to override that, and `exclude` to drop specific pages.
A category also lists places that are not areas of its zone: a city that is a zone
of its own (Orgrimmar in Durotar), or an area of a neighbour (Ruins of Alterac in
Hillsbrad). Those are excluded, so each place has one line, under the zone the
client puts it in. Passages that join two places (Deeprun Tram, a city's gates)
stay at both ends.
Covers all 46 Classic Era zone maps. Azeroth (947), Kalimdor (1414) and
Eastern Kingdoms (1415) are deliberately absent: they are not Zone-type maps,
a click on them is Blizzard's own navigation, and UI/SubzoneClick.lua ignores
non-Zone maps anyway.
44 of the 46 resolve from the zone name directly. The two exceptions are The
Barrens and The Hinterlands, where the wiki drops the leading article. For the
Barrens the vanilla 'Barrens subzones' category (34 pages) is correct, NOT the
Cataclysm-split 'Northern Barrens subzones' (28).
`aliases` maps a name the CLIENT reports to the wiki page title, for cases
where normalisation is not enough to make them meet. Normalisation already
handles case, a leading 'the', and apostrophes, so 'The Bulwark' finds the
page titled 'Bulwark' with no alias needed. Use `/spz debug` in-game to see
the raw name the client reports for an area.

aliases._comment: parent uiMapID -> { client-reported name: wiki page title }
